newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold Fields says Q2 hit by lower gold price.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields says Q2 hit by lower gold price.

text.p: Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd said on Thursday that second quarter profit had been hit by the lower gold price as well as by the Easter holidays which disrupted production.
"Revenue was all down because of the gold price," said Keith Spencer, general manager of Gold Fields gold operations.
But he added that working costs had held more or less steady and that this had capped profit declines.
"This was a very pleasing result. Working costs stayed more or less the same," Spencer said.

Gold Fields' stable of mines received an average gold price of 49,411 rand/kg in the June quarter, compared to 51,737 in the preceding March quarter. Unit working costs were 41,611 rand/kg compared to 41,593 rand/kg.
But Spencer expressed concern at the shrinking gap between working costs and the gold price. "That gap over there is concerning and is coming down," he said.
With the bullion price currently at 12-year lows, more pressure is expected on South African gold mines.

Gold Fields made a pre-capex net profit of 192.34 million rand compared to 236.42 million rand in the previous quarter. Capital expenditure for the second quarter was 230.49 million rand compared to the first quarter's 205.88 million rand.

The scheme of arrangement whereby Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's Elandsrand Gold Mining Co Ltd will acquire Gold Fields' Deelkraal Gold Mining Co Ltd should be concluded by mid October, the group said.
Spencer said that Deelkraal had changed the focus of its capital expenditure and was focusing on projects that were of mutual benefit to both itself and Elandsrand.
